blocks.p: **What it is:** a nine-digit number you need in order to work, to open accounts, and for taxes. **It is free** — nobody takes money from you for it.

blocks.warn: **Read this first — it may save you a whole trip.** If you have an immigration application pending, or you are about to file one — work permit (I-765), residency (I-485), family reunification, or naturalization (N-400) — **ask for the Social Security number from inside the application itself.** Every one of these forms has a Social Security box. Check it, and the number comes to you in the mail after approval — no visit, no appointment, no line.

blocks.h: If that is not your situation

ul: **Wait ten days** after you arrive, so your records reach the system
Start the application at [ssa.gov/number-card](https://www.ssa.gov/number-card), then go to the nearest office with your documents
The form: [Form SS-5](https://www.ssa.gov/forms/ss-5.pdf) — **and the application is free**, which is written on the form itself
Nearest office: [ssa.gov/locator](https://secure.ssa.gov/ICON/main.jsp) · or an appointment at [1-800-772-1213](tel:+18007721213)

blocks.do: At `ssa.gov/locator`: type your ZIP code, and the result is the nearest office address and its hours.

blocks.h: What to bring — originals, not copies

ul: A valid passport for identity
A valid status document: the green card (I-551), or I-94, or the work permit (I-766)
And proof of age — a birth certificate if you have one

blocks.alert: **The original, or a certified copy from the agency that issued the paper — nothing else.** Photocopies are not accepted. **A copy notarized by a notary is not accepted either** — back home "certification" means the notary, but at Social Security it means **the agency that issued the paper itself**. This is why many people are turned away at the door.

blocks.warn: **And a free interpreter on the phone.** The agency says it provides interpreter services free of charge: you call [1-800-772-1213](tel:+18007721213) and stay on the line until a representative reaches you, and they connect an interpreter. If you need to come to the office, they book you an appointment and bring an interpreter. [Details](https://www.ssa.gov/multilanguage/interpreter.html)

blocks.p: **The agency's Arabic page** has about twenty publications on it, including the instructions for Form SS-5: [ssa.gov/multilanguage/arabic](https://www.ssa.gov/multilanguage/arabic.html)
**Time:** the card arrives in the mail within **5 to 10 business days**. If three weeks pass, call the number above.
**And if you are not eligible:** there is an alternative for taxes called **ITIN** — see the banking section.

t: Where to Live — Choosing Your Area

blocks.p: **You can change the house; you cannot change the area.** A lease is one year and then you move — **but the school, the drive to work, and the flooding live with you the whole year.**
**These standards work for any city**, and the tools under them are for the Houston area.

blocks.h: 1) Safety — and start here

blocks.p: **Three official sites, and no fourth.** ⚠️ **Avoid sites that give a neighborhood a safety score out of 100** — how they calculate it is not public, and they mix crime with income and who lives there, **so they brand whole neighborhoods with a number you cannot trace.**

rows: [Houston Police crime map](https://communitycrimemap.com) — opened from the [official police page](https://www.houstontx.gov/police/cs/Community_Crime_Map_hosted_by_LexisNexis.htm)
[Police data by street](https://www.houstontx.gov/police/cs/Monthly_Crime_Data_by_Street_and_Police_Beat.htm) — free monthly files going back to 2009

blocks.do: And in every one of these maps: type the address or the street name, then read **the last year**, not the last week — the result is dots on a map, each one carrying the type of report and its date. **And compare your street to the street next to it, not a city to a city.**

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **Outside the city limits there is no map.** I searched the Harris County Sheriff's Office site and found no public crime map — **so if you live in an area that is not part of a city, you will find no data about your street.** **That is one more reason to go see the street yourself.**

blocks.h: How to read the map — in the police's own words

blocks.warn: **Houston Police write on their site:** the map **"does not reflect or certify 'safe' or 'unsafe' areas"**, and "areas with a high volume of foot traffic, vehicle traffic, and if densely populated **may have more reported crimes than other areas. This does not necessarily mean more crime occurs there, but that more crime is reported there.**"

blocks.p: ⚠️ **This is the most important sentence in this section:** a street with restaurants and shops fills up with dots, **and an empty lot looks clean** — and whoever compares the two runs away from the better one.

ul: **Compare a street to the street next to it**, not a city to a city
**Look at the type of crime, not the number** — a car theft is not a home break-in
**Take the last year**, not the last week
**Then visit the street in the evening**, not at midday only — **no map tells you what you feel while you are standing in it.**

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **No official source anywhere gives crime counts by ZIP code** — not federal, not the state, not the police. **Houston Police say it in their own words: "ZIP code boundaries and police beat boundaries do not correspond... ZIP codes are provided only as a reference."** **So the number you see on a site that asks for your ZIP code is not a count — it is an estimate produced by a model.** And the Census Bureau says a ZIP Code is a mail delivery route, not a place on a map.

blocks.h: The state registry — by address

blocks.p: The State of Texas publishes a public registry **you can search by address or by ZIP code, free**: [state registry](https://publicsite.dps.texas.gov/SexOffenderRegistry) — and the Department of Public Safety says: **"State law specifically makes most information in this database freely available to the public."**

blocks.do: Type the address or the ZIP code, and the result is a list of who is registered in that range, with an approximate address for each name.

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **Their warning is written on the site, and it is passed on as it stands:** **"Anyone who uses any information on this website to injure, harass, or for any other unlawful purpose may be subject to criminal prosecution or civil liability."**

blocks.h: 2) Flooding — and here the law is on your side

blocks.alert: **A house that is two hundred dollars cheaper than its neighbors may be cheaper because it flooded.** ⚠️ **It never crosses a newcomer's mind that Houston has areas that flood every two years** — this one point alone can save a family its savings.

blocks.alt: **Find the flood zone for your address:** [the official FEMA map](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/search) — type the address, and the result is the zone letter.

blocks.h: Start with the federal map

ul: Open the [federal flood map center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/search) **and type in the address** — free, and it takes minutes
**Zones that start with the letter A or V are high risk** (Special Flood Hazard Area), **X is moderate or low**, and D means the risk has not been studied
And for Harris County alone: [Flood Education Mapping Tool](https://www.harriscountyfemt.org/) — search by address, and it shows the flood zone boundaries

blocks.do: At `msc.fema.gov`: the address goes in the field labelled `Enter an address, place, or coordinates` — and the result is a map with the zone letter on it. At `harriscountyfemt.org`: the field itself shows you the shape of the address it wants — `9900 Northwest Fwy., Houston, TX 77092`.

ul: **har.com is where you will browse the listings — and it tells you nothing about flooding.** The association removed that from listings in February 2026, **so do not assume a listing's silence means the house never flooded** — its [har.com/flood](https://www.har.com/flood) page is a list of links pointing you to the same sources

**Buyers Aware** — a free tool from an institute at Texas A&M, funded by the state emergency management division. You type the address and it gives you a flood and fire risk assessment **for that property**: [buyersaware.org](https://buyersaware.org) — **it covers the areas Hurricane Harvey hit**

blocks.do: At `buyersaware.org`: type the address, and the result is a risk assessment **for the property itself**, not for the neighborhood. **And `har.com/flood` is a page of links, not a tool — there is nothing to type in it.**

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **The FEMA map remains the legal reference** — insurance and the seller's disclosure both rest on it. **Everything else is an estimate that helps you; none of it replaces the map.**

blocks.h: And the law requires the landlord to tell you

blocks.warn: **Texas law — Property Code §92.0135:** the landlord must give you a notice that says **whether the unit is inside the 100-year floodplain**, and **whether any part of it has flooded at least once in the last five years**.

blocks.p: **And the text of the notice itself tells you:** **"Most tenant insurance policies do not cover damages or loss incurred in a flood. You should seek insurance coverage that would cover losses caused by a flood."**

rows: At the signing of the lease or before it — **and both parties sign it together**
A clause in the lease, an addendum, or a separate sheet

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **The rule changed on September 1, 2025** — before that the notice had to be **a separate sheet**; now it may be a clause in the lease. **Signatures from both parties are required either way.**

blocks.h: And if the landlord breaks the rule

blocks.p: **If he did not give you the notice and then your belongings suffered a substantial loss in a flood, you can end the lease** with written notice **within 30 days** of the damage, **and the landlord returns to you all the rent you paid in advance** within 30 days of the termination.
⚠️ **And substantial loss is defined in the law:** the cost to repair or replace reaches **50% or more** of the value of your belongings on the day of the flood.

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **And there is no website that tells you whether this particular house flooded.** I searched and did not find a single official tool that does it. **The only way is to ask the landlord — and the law requires him to answer in writing.** **So do not accept a spoken answer.**

blocks.h: Insurance — and thirty days

ul: **Ordinary renter's insurance does not cover flooding** — the coverage is a separate policy: [National Flood Insurance Program](https://www.floodsmart.gov/get-insured/buy-a-policy)
⚠️ **And the coverage starts 30 days after you buy it** — **so whoever buys it with the storm already coming bought it too late**
**And a renter buys contents coverage only** — up to 100,000 dollars for belongings

blocks.h: 3) The road to work — by time, not by miles

blocks.p: **Twenty miles in Houston can be an hour.** Try the road **at work hours, not at midday**, and add it up: gas + toll roads + two hours of your day, every day.

ul: By public transit: [METRO Trip Planner](https://planyourtrip.ridemetro.org/) — point to point, by hour and by day
**Toll roads:** [hctra.org](https://www.hctra.org) — **and there is no official calculator for the trip**, so work out your trip and multiply it by 44 trips a month

blocks.do: In the METRO planner: type your starting point and your destination, **then set the time to 7 in the morning on a weekday** — and the result is the trip length and the number of transfers. **And `hctra.org` has no calculator: you read the price of each segment and add them up yourself.**

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **And there are two official sites, no more:** [hctra.org](https://www.hctra.org) and [txtag.org](https://www.txtag.org). **Around them are copycat sites with similar names** — and the agency never sends a payment link by text message.

blocks.h: 4) The school — the campus, not the district

blocks.p: **Two schools in one school district can be very different.** So search for **the school by name**, not for the district.

ul: The official rating: [txschools.gov](https://txschools.gov/) — **search by address or by school name**
**And the 2026 ratings came out on August 14, 2026**, along with earlier years — **so the data is available and current**

blocks.do: At `txschools.gov`: type the address or the school name, and the result is a grade from `A` to `F`. **The grade is for that school alone — not for the neighborhood, and not for the whole district.**

blocks.h: And which school will my child be enrolled in

blocks.p: ⚠️ **And there is no single tool for the whole state** — each school district publishes its own:

blocks.do: All three district tools work from the address: you type the address of the house and it gives you **the name of the school assigned to it** — elementary, middle, and high. **Then you take that name to `txschools.gov` to read its grade.**

blocks.h: 5) Property tax and MUD — and it reaches you in the rent

blocks.p: **Two neighboring suburbs can be thousands of dollars a year apart.** The reason is that one of them is inside a **utility district (MUD)** that collects its tax **on top of the county and school tax**.

**And the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality defines it:** a district created to provide **water, sewer, and drainage** inside its boundaries — **and its taxes are levied "on all property in the district based on appraised value—regardless of the services received by each landowner."**

blocks.h: And the difference is not small — the adopted 2025 rates

rows: 1.1100 — **about three times the county tax by itself**

ul: Search by address: [Harris County tax database](https://harris.trueprodigy-taxtransparency.com/taxTransparency/propertySearch) — **it shows every entity that taxes the property and how much**
And the table of rates: [Harris County Tax Office](https://www.hctax.net/property/jurisdictiontaxrates) — the MUDs are in it too
And in Fort Bend: [esearch.fbcad.org](https://esearch.fbcad.org/) for the value, [texas.gov/PropertyTaxes](https://www.texas.gov/PropertyTaxes) for the rates

blocks.do: In the tax database: type the address, and the result is a list of every entity that taxes this property and the rate of each. **And every line with `MUD` in it is a charge on top of the county and school taxes, not instead of them.**

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **You are a renter, so why does this concern you?** Because the landlord pays it **and counts it into the rent**. **And two similar apartments with two different rents may differ by tax, not by size.**

blocks.h: 6) And Houston has no zoning — and this shocks every newcomer

blocks.warn: **The City of Houston writes on its official site:** **"The City of Houston does not have zoning, but development is governed by ordinance codes that address how property can be subdivided."**

blocks.p: ⚠️ **And what it means in practice:** a shop or a warehouse can be built next to your house. **And the city itself says:** "In Houston, where property is not governed by deed restrictions, **a property owner may be free to operate a commercial business in the neighborhood.**"

blocks.h: And the alternative: deed restrictions

ul: **Ask: does this neighborhood have deed restrictions?** — they are written agreements that limit what may be done with the property
**And you get a copy of them from the county clerk** — Harris County Clerk, [713.755.6405](tel:+17137556405) — and bring the property description, the lot, and the block
⚠️ **And the city itself helps enforce them** — this is unusual, and it is what makes up for the absence of zoning

blocks.h: 7) And how close you are to your community

blocks.p: **A mosque or a church · a halal market · a doctor who speaks Arabic · an Arabic school.** ⚠️ **And the Arabna directory answers these itself** — open the directory and type in the address; you do not need an outside site.

blocks.h: 8) And if you are buying, not renting

blocks.p: **Three things are added, and all of them come before signing:**

rows: Property Code §5.008 — **requires him to disclose past flooding, insurance claims, FEMA assistance, and where the property stands in relation to the flood zone**
**Seven days to end the contract for any reason** if the disclosure reaches you after signing
Ask for the yearly figure, not just whether they exist

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **And the disclosure is not required in every case:** a new house never lived in before, foreclosure homes, and transfers of ownership between relatives — **all are exempt.** **So whoever buys a new house gets no disclosure, and has to check for himself.**

blocks.h: And a list to walk through while you stand in front of the house

blocks.p: **Ten questions, in order — and next to each question, where to find its answer.**

rows: 1 · Is the address in a flood zone?
2 · Has the house flooded in the last five years?
**Ask the landlord — and the law requires a signed answer**
3 · What is the crime situation on this street?
4 · And what is in the state registry at this address?
5 · How long does the road take at work hours?
6 · And how much do the toll roads cost per month?
7 · What is my child's school called and what is its rating?
8 · Is the address inside a MUD?
9 · Does the neighborhood have deed restrictions?
10 · And how far is the nearest mosque or church and halal market?

blocks.alert: ⚠️ **And one of the ten is worth leaving the house over: the second.** **And its answer is your right by the text of the law, not a favor you ask for.**

blocks.p: **Then visit the street in the evening before you sign.** ⚠️ **And no site on this list tells you what ten minutes standing there will tell you.**

blocks.warn: **The Fair Housing Act makes it illegal to turn you down because of:** your country of origin · your religion · your race · your sex · having children · disability. Anyone who tells you "we don't rent to Arabs" or "we don't rent to women in hijab" has broken a federal law — **it is not a matter of taste**.

blocks.h: The deadline — know it before you think about filing

rows: **One year** from the incident — after that it is not accepted
**Two years** from the last incident — even if the HUD deadline has passed
Complaint to the state of Texas

blocks.p: **And if the wrong is ongoing** — a standing policy, not a single incident — **the year counts from the last time it happened**, and that opens a door for many people who thought it was closed.

ul: Filing: [hud.gov/reporthousingdiscrimination](https://www.hud.gov/reporthousingdiscrimination) · [1-800-669-9777](tel:+18006699777)
**You do not need a lawyer to file a complaint**, and the complaint is free

**HUD publishes the complaint form and its instructions in Arabic**, and says that if you call and do not speak English **they will bring an interpreter in your language onto the call**: [Forms in other languages](https://www.hud.gov/stat/fheo/complaint-filing-nonenglish)

blocks.do: The complaint is filed on the site or by phone, and it needs three things: **the date of what happened, the address of the property, and the name of the landlord or the company.** Have them ready before you start.

blocks.h: Section 8 — and the question itself is different

blocks.alert: **There is no paper form, and there is no application that is always open.** The waiting list **opens for short periods and then closes** — the public housing list opened in the summer of 2026 by lottery and closed after about 56,000 applications. **Anyone who was not registered on the day it opened misses the whole round.**

rows: Houston Housing Authority — its new name is Housing Alliance HTX · [(713) 260-0500](tel:+17132600500)

blocks.do: Both lists open on announced dates and then close — **open the link to find out whether it is open today**, and no paper application is accepted.

blocks.p: **Watch the name:** the older printed material says Houston Housing Authority, the newer says Housing Alliance HTX — **they are one and the same agency**.
**And a right you have:** both agencies receive federal funding, **so you have the right to ask them for language help**.

blocks.h: What the landlord usually asks for

ul: A credit check and a rental history report — it has your addresses, your income, and any eviction cases
Proof of income: a pay stub or a letter from work
A deposit — and it can go up if your record is weak

blocks.h: And if you have no credit history

blocks.p: **Be honest with yourself: no law requires a landlord to accept any substitute.** Here is what renters offer, and some landlords accept:

ul: A co-signer who signs with you
A bigger deposit, or paying some months up front
A letter from your employer with your salary, and bank statements that show your income is steady

blocks.warn: **And a federal right nobody knows about:** if your application is denied because of a report, the landlord **is required** to tell you and give you the company's name, address, and phone number. **You get a free copy of the report within 60 days**, and the company has **30 days** to investigate your dispute. **Errors in these reports are common, and they do get corrected.** And your credit report is free once a year: [AnnualCreditReport.com](https://www.annualcreditreport.com) · [877-322-8228](tel:+18773228228)

blocks.do: At `AnnualCreditReport.com`: it asks for your name, your address, and your Social Security number, then questions about your financial history to verify you. **It never asks for a bank card — if you are asked for one, you are on a different site.**

blocks.h: The deposit and keeping up the home

ul: The owner has **thirty days** to return the deposit after you move out, **and a penalty of three times the amount** if it is held back in bad faith
**Ask for a written receipt, and photograph the home the day you move in** — the photos are your proof the day you move out
**And if you end up in a dispute with him: move fast and do not wait years**, and talk to a lawyer or a free legal aid service

blocks.p: **And before you sign:** the signed lease is what governs, not talk. Write anything you were promised out loud **into the lease**, and ask for a copy before signing day so you can read it calmly.
**Know this first:** the license comes **from the state, not from the federal government**. This section is about **Texas**.

blocks.h: What Texas accepts today

blocks.p: **A valid passport + a visa + a valid I-94.** This is written at the Department of Public Safety: [Lawful presence page](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/us-citizenship-or-lawful-presence-requirement)

blocks.alert:
**And a warning:** the department **has proposed a change** requiring **the visa itself to be valid**, rather than expired with a valid I-94. **It has not been adopted yet**, and the official page still carries the old wording. **So check the page before you rely on an expired visa.**
The department has two official pages that say different things about the visa, and we quote both without choosing between them:
· “Lawful presence” page: visa may be valid or expired, with a valid I-94 (page dated September 22, 2020 · accessed September 1, 2026)
· “Identification requirements” page: valid, unexpired visa (page dated September 22, 2020 · accessed September 1, 2026)
The Texas Department of Public Safety decides; ask them through their [contact page](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/contact-us) before your appointment.

blocks.h: The forms

blocks.p: **And the youngest age for a learner license is 15**, and the parent or guardian must be present, or send an application signed by him before a notary.

blocks.h: And the appointment is required

blocks.p: The department says: **all license services are by appointment only.** Booking: [public.txdpsscheduler.com](https://public.txdpsscheduler.com/)

blocks.do: Before you book, have three things ready: **the type of service, the office, and a phone number the confirmation can reach you on.** **Appointments get cancelled and slots open up — so check the site more than once a day.**

blocks.h: The steps

ul: Proof of identity and status, and **two documents** that prove your address in Texas
Vision test · written test · learner license · road test
**And your foreign license** is fine for a visit, **but the time it is accepted once you become a resident is short** — check right away, not a month from now

blocks.h: And a driving school cuts two steps short for you — for a fee

blocks.p: **This saves weeks of waiting, and few people know it:**

ul: **The road test at the school itself.** The department approves driving schools to give the driving test for a Class C license — **so you do not wait for a department appointment**. ⚠️ **And the fee here is set by the school, not the department**, and in the department's words: "Fees charged by a driving school for the driving test are not regulated by the Department" — **so ask about the price before you book, and compare two schools**. [Third-party skills testing program](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/third-party-skills-testing-program)

**And the written test is waived for you if you take it inside the course.** In the department's words: **"The written test is waived for anyone who took it during a driver education course"**. ⚠️ **And ask the school directly: is the written test inside the course?** — because not all courses are like that. [Choosing a driver education course](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/choosing-driver-education-course)

blocks.warn: **And who has to take the course in the first place:** • **Ages 18 to 24** getting a first license in Texas — **the six-hour adult course is required** • **And 25 and older** — **no course required**, but you can take one so you can do both tests at the school • **And under 18** — the full driver education course

blocks.h: As for the other states

blocks.p: **Some states issue a license regardless of immigration status, and Texas is not one of them.**

blocks.alert: **And do not rely on a list people pass around.** The rules change from year to year, **and some of what is issued is a "driving card" rather than a full license**, and it does not work as federal ID. **So read the motor vehicle department website of that state itself before you travel there for a license.**

blocks.h: The federal license (REAL ID)

ul: The compliant one has **a star in the top corner**
You need it to fly inside the country and to enter federal buildings
**And you can travel with your passport instead of it**

blocks.h: And two deadlines that start the day you arrive

rows: To get a Texas license after you move
To register your car — after that, fines

blocks.alert: **And the order matters:** the department requires the **car to be registered in Texas before** you apply for the license.

blocks.h: Don't drive? You can get an ID card

blocks.p: **You still need official ID** — for the bank, the hospital, and the school. The department issues an **ID card for non-drivers**, and it accepts **the same lawful presence documents** accepted for the license.

rows: For anyone under 60 — valid six years
And two documents to prove where you live
And the "thirty days in Texas" requirement does not apply to anyone who surrenders a valid license from another state

blocks.warn: **Every child in America has the right to a public school education, whatever the family's immigration status.** The Supreme Court ruling (Plyler v. Doe) is still in force.

blocks.h: What the school is not allowed to do

ul: ✕ Ask you about your immigration status as a condition of enrollment
✕ Refuse a foreign birth certificate
✕ Block enrollment because you would not give a Social Security number — **giving it is optional**, and the school has to tell you so

blocks.h: What it really does ask for

ul: **Proof of residence** — a lease or a bill, to set which school
**Proof of the child's age** — the birth certificate
**Immunization record**

blocks.h: Your right to an interpreter — the most important part of this section

blocks.p: **Your right stands.** Federal guidance papers were withdrawn in 2025 and 2026, **and in July 2026 a regulation was struck out** — one that allowed a complaint about the **outcome** of a policy without proving intent to discriminate. **The two laws that carry your right were not touched** — and they stand on their own:

rows: The Equal Educational Opportunities Act — **an act of Congress**, and a parent can sue under it directly · **this is the strongest thing you hold**
Education Code Section 29.056(d): notice **in English and in the parent's first language** · and **your written consent** before your child enters a language program or leaves it
The Civil Rights Act of 1964 — bars discrimination by national origin · **and its path is harder since July 2026**

blocks.alert: **The interpreting is free, and from a competent person.** **Your son, your brother, or your friend may not be asked to interpret for you** — and neither may an untrained staff member. A child who interprets for his parents in a meeting about his own grades or behavior **is put in a place he cannot carry**.

blocks.p: **Ask for it in writing, and keep a dated copy.** If you are refused, start with the nearest office: the **Bilingual/ESL department in your school district**, then the district administration — **and your written request is what becomes your evidence if you escalate**. The federal complaint stays open: the Office for Civil Rights at the Department of Education — [1-800-872-5327](tel:+18008725327) · [File a complaint](https://www.ed.gov/laws-and-policy/civil-rights-laws/file-complaint) — **and it has been harder since July 2026: you must prove intent to discriminate, not show its outcome.**

blocks.h: English language support

ul: **A right, not an extra service**, and the school must tell you where your child stands within **30 days**
**School meals:** the application **does not require citizenship**, and the form has a box to say you have no Social Security number. Many schools serve them free to everyone — **ask first**

blocks.h: Immunizations — and where to get them free

rows: Birth to 18 years · for the uninsured · [888-777-5320](tel:+18887775320)
**Immigration status is not one of the eligibility conditions**
No one is denied service for being unable to pay
[(832) 927-7350](tel:+18329277350) — and it posts immunization schedules in Arabic

blocks.p: **The list of immunizations the school requires** changes every year: [Requirements page](https://www.dshs.texas.gov/immunizations/school/requirements)

**Immunizations your child got in your home country are accepted** if the documentation is clear. **If the record is lost** — a new schedule is started, or **a blood test that proves immunity** instead of repeating the shots.

blocks.h: Public pre-K — free for a child who does not speak English

blocks.warn: **Is your four-year-old still not speaking English? Public pre-K is free for him.** Inability to speak English **is an eligibility category on its own** in the Education Code — **with no income condition**. The school checks it **with a language test for the child**, not with a paper from you.

blocks.p: **Enrollment starts in the spring for the fall year** — so ask your school district early. **Private pre-K in Houston costs thousands of dollars a year.**

blocks.h: Staying with family or friends? Your children start school right away

blocks.warn: **If you are living temporarily with your brother or your friend because you lost your housing or cannot afford the rent — your children are enrolled right away.** **No lease, no bill, no immunization record.** Federal law tells the school to **enroll the child immediately, even if the child cannot produce the records normally required — school records, immunizations, and proof of residence.**

ul: **And with it school transportation** to his first school, **and free meals automatically**, with no application
Ask the school for a form called the **Student Residency Questionnaire**
And if they refuse: the Texas Education Agency — [complaintsmanagement@tea.texas.gov](mailto:complaintsmanagement@tea.texas.gov) · [(512) 463-3544](tel:+15124633544)

blocks.alert: **The condition is that the shared housing is because of lost housing or hard times** — not for someone who chose to live with family while able to live elsewhere.

blocks.h: A Social Security number is not required to enroll

blocks.p: **Did the school ask you for the Social Security card? Giving it is optional.** The Texas Education Agency says that **the district gives the student an alternative identification number when no Social Security number is provided.**

rows: The records required by law are three
Birth certificate or proof of identity · previous school records · immunization record
And the federal Department of Education
A student may not be denied enrollment if the student or the parent chooses not to provide a Social Security number

blocks.alert: **And he is not refused for having no birth certificate, or because his papers point to a foreign place of birth.**

blocks.h: School meals

blocks.p: **Breakfast is free for every HISD student.** Lunch **is free for everyone in most schools but not all** — and in certain schools you have to submit an application. **Check your own child's school, and apply even if you think you do not qualify.**

t: A bank account with no Social Security number

blocks.p: **The good news: this is allowed.** Federal law lets the bank open an account with any one of these: a tax number (**ITIN**) · **a passport number** and the country that issued it · a foreign ID card · or any government document with a photo.
**But the law allows it; it does not require it.** Every bank sets its own policy — **so call and ask before you go**: “Do you open an account with a passport or an ITIN?”

blocks.h: The ITIN — what it is

ul: A number from the tax agency for someone who needs to file a return and is not eligible for a Social Security number
**It is given regardless of immigration status**
**And it does not grant work permission and does not change your status** — it is for taxes only
To apply: [Form W-7](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fw7.pdf) · [Instructions](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/iw7.pdf)
**Time: about seven weeks** — and nine to eleven in tax season

blocks.alert: **Do not mail your original passport.** Go to an IRS Taxpayer Assistance Center (IRS TAC) with an appointment, or use an authorized agent who hands your papers back to you on the spot.

blocks.warn: **And there is no Arabic version of the form or of its instructions.** The tax agency publishes in eight languages, **and Arabic is not one of them** — so do not waste your time looking for it.

blocks.p: **And watch out:** with no tax number the bank may open only **a non-interest account** for you — because interest with no number has 24% tax taken out of it.

blocks.h: Stay away from

ul: **Check cashing stores** — their fees eat your pay month after month
**Prepaid cards** — their protection if you lose them is **weaker** than a bank account's
**And carrying cash** — it gets lost and does not come back

blocks.p: **And ask for a Bank On certified account** — opens with $25 or less, monthly fee $5 or less, **and zero overdraft fees**. [joinbankon.org](https://joinbankon.org)

blocks.do: The list is of certified **accounts**, not of banks — **so ask at the branch by the name of the account itself**, not "do you have Bank On?"

blocks.warn: **This is the section that changes the most.** The rules changed in 2025 and 2026. What is here is **the road**; who qualifies is what changes — check [healthcare.gov](https://www.healthcare.gov) or ask a free navigator.

blocks.h: Four ways to get coverage

ul: **Through work** — this is how most people get it. Ask your employer on the first day
**The insurance Marketplace** — [healthcare.gov](https://www.healthcare.gov) · [1-800-318-2596](tel:+18003182596)
**Medicaid and CHIP** — for people with low income and for children
**Buying directly** from an insurance company

blocks.do: At `healthcare.gov`: type your ZIP code, your household size, and your expected income for the year — **and the price you see is the price after the subsidy, not the full price.**

blocks.h: And the enrollment date matters

ul: Open enrollment **starts November 1** every year
**And the final deadline changes** — check the website, and do not rely on a date you heard
**And Medicaid and CHIP have no deadline** — apply any time

blocks.warn: **And this one is about you in particular:** moving to America from another country opens a **Special Enrollment Period** for you — you can enroll outside open enrollment. **It lasts 60 days. Do not miss it.**

blocks.h: And even if you do not qualify — you are not without care

ul: **Community health centers:** their fees go **by your income**, **and no patient is turned away for being unable to pay**. [findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov](https://findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov) · [877-464-4772](tel:+18774644772)

**And emergency care is everyone's right:** the EMTALA law requires any hospital to examine you and stabilize you, **and it has no right to turn you away** because you have no insurance or cannot pay **or are not a citizen**
**And Emergency Medicaid** covers the emergency — childbirth included — for anyone who meets the state's conditions, **regardless of immigration status**

blocks.do: Type the address or the ZIP code, and the result is the centers near you. **And when you book, ask for the "sliding fee" by name** — that is what makes the price match your income.

blocks.alert: **And a right that is in force today:** the interpreter at the hospital and the clinic is **free** — under a rule that became enforceable in **July 2025**: language assistance services are provided free of charge, and **a patient may not be required to bring their own interpreter or pay for one**, **and a child is not used as an interpreter** except in a narrow emergency. **And this did not change with what changed in 2025 and 2026.**

blocks.h: And the help with choosing is free

blocks.p: **The Navigator** is trained **and required to be neutral**, **and the service is completely free** — do not pay anyone to enroll you. [healthcare.gov/find-local-help](https://www.healthcare.gov/find-local-help/)

blocks.do: Type the ZIP code to see who can help you face to face. **The help is free — and anyone who asks you for a fee is not one of them.**

blocks.p: **And the insurance agent** explains and enrolls you **and stays your contact after that** — and if a bill is denied you call him instead of fighting with the company yourself. **And ask him on the first call: “Do I owe you any fees?”** — his commission usually comes from the company, not from you.

blocks.h: And with no insurance in Harris County — this is the door

blocks.p: **It is called the Harris Health Financial Assistance Program**, and it used to be known as the **Gold Card**. **Eligibility in their policy is two conditions:** living in the county, and income.
**And the form accepts a foreign consulate card** as proof of identity, **and it has an Undocumented box among the status choices.**

**And outside Harris County:** every county has a similar program — Fort Bend · [281-341-6624](tel:+12813416624) — **but it is much narrower:** income at 21% of the poverty line, and savings under $2,000.

blocks.h: And the emergency room is not urgent care

blocks.p: **The emergency room costs two to three times the clinic** for the same treatment. **And urgent care is the middle ground** for what is not life threatening.

blocks.alert: **But for what threatens life — chest pain, trouble breathing, a serious injury — it is the emergency room or 911, and do not think about the cost in that moment.**

blocks.h: And two numbers to save before you need them

rows: [1-800-222-1222](tel:+18002221222) — free and confidential · and in 161 languages · a doctor or a pharmacist answers
[988](tel:+1988) — and say the word “Arabic” in English when they answer, and an interpreter reaches you in about twenty seconds

blocks.p: **Why it matters:** explaining your pain in your own language is not a luxury. **A mistake in describing a symptom changes the diagnosis.**

ul: **At the clinic and the hospital, interpreting is your right and it is free** — ask for it, **and do not rely on your son to interpret your illness**
And in our Arabna directory, the businesses whose staff speak Arabic **are marked with a tag** — use the filter
And ask before the appointment: **Do you take my insurance?**

blocks.warn: **And if you have no insurance, ask this question word for word:** “Are your fees based on income?” Many clinics lower the fee for people with low income, **and some take nothing at all** — **and this is not offered to you; you are the one who has to ask.**

ul: In the directory, halal butchers and markets **are marked with a tag** — use the filter
And ask at the store: **fully halal, or a halal section inside a general store?**
And many Arabic markets sell **meat, produce, and Arabic bread together** — so one trip is enough

t: Home utilities: electricity, gas, water, and internet

blocks.p: **The first question to ask before you sign the lease:** **which utilities are on my account, and which ones are inside the rent?** — **The answer is different from one home to the next.**

blocks.warn: **If you are in an apartment complex, this one is about you:** many complexes **put water, sewer, and trash inside the rent** or split them among the residents as a fixed monthly amount, **and some include gas as well**. **Electricity is usually on you.** **So ask before you sign, and ask for it in writing in the lease** — nobody is held to what was only said out loud.

blocks.h: 1) Electricity — the first thing you do

ul: **Start on it before moving day.** In Texas **electricity does not come with the home** — you open the account in your own name. **People who moved in before doing that spent the night with no power**
**It is an open market** — you compare companies, choose one, and switch if you want
**Read the contract length** — leaving early carries a penalty
You may be asked for a **deposit** because you have no credit history, **and it is returned to you** after a stretch of paying on time
**Ask what the alternative is** if they ask you for a Social Security number — do not assume the answer is no

blocks.h: 2) Gas

ul: **Not an open market like electricity** — usually one company serves your area
**And many apartments have no gas at all** — all electric, so there is no third account on you
**Ask: is there gas in this place? And who pays for it?**

blocks.h: 3) Water, sewer, and trash

ul: **In a single-family house:** an account in your name with the city
**In a complex:** usually **inside the rent or split among the residents** — **ask roughly how much it runs a month**, because the split amount surprises a lot of people

blocks.h: 4) Internet — because you don't get much choice

ul: **One or two providers serve your address**, and you may have only one in front of you. **Search by your address first**
**Ask the company directly: "Do you have a plan for low-income households?"** — many of them do and don't advertise it
**In some complexes the internet is inside the rent** with one particular provider — **ask before you sign up on your own account**
**And the ACP program has ended** — don't look for it, and don't believe anyone who offers it to you

blocks.h: Help with energy bills — LIHEAP

ul: It helps with heating and cooling bills, **and it stops your service from being cut off**
[Program information](https://acf.gov/ocs/programs/liheap) · [1-866-674-6327](tel:+18666746327) (business days)
**Careful: this program does require a particular legal status** — unlike school meals

blocks.warn: Assistance programs can touch the "public charge" rules. **Talk to an immigration lawyer if you have an application pending.**

blocks.p: **Insurance is required in Texas.** The minimum is `30,000 / 60,000 / 25,000` (injury to one person / injuries per crash / property damage).

blocks.h: Inspection — this changed, so read it even if you have been here for years

blocks.alert: **The annual safety inspection was ended in Texas as of January 1, 2025** for non-commercial vehicles, **and a fee paid with your registration took its place: $7.50 a year** ($16.75 for a new vehicle with a two-year registration).

blocks.p: **But the emissions test is still required in `Harris County`** — along with `Fort Bend`, `Montgomery`, `Galveston`, and `Brazoria`. It is done **once a year** for vehicles from two to 24 years old, **and within 90 days before you register**.

**So the short of it:** in `Harris County` you go to an inspection station once a year — **but it is an emissions test only, not a safety inspection** — then **you renew your registration online** once it passes.

blocks.do: Inspection stations are searched by ZIP code. **And renewing online needs your license plate number and the last four digits of the `VIN`** — both are on the registration paper you already have.

blocks.p: **The transfer is filed at the county tax assessor-collector's office within thirty days of the purchase.** **The renewal window** runs from 90 days before it expires until 12 months after, **and you may drive for five business days past the expiration without a ticket**, and after that the fine reaches up to 200 dollars.

blocks.h: A gap in your insurance — the most dangerous paragraph in this whole guide

blocks.alert: **If you fall behind on a payment and your policy is cancelled:** • **Coverage ends as of the cancellation date** • You can ask to have it reinstated within **sixty days** — **but reinstating is the company's choice, not its duty** • **The policy is not in force again until the day the company receives the money** • **And the days in between are not covered** — even if the policy is reinstated afterward

blocks.p: **What this means in a word: one single day with no insurance is enough.** Anyone who has a crash during those days **is treated as a driver with no insurance** — even if he holds a valid policy today. **So pay before the cancellation date, not after, and do not lean on the sixty-day window.**
**You are asked for proof of insurance in two places:** when you register the car — **and without proof it is not registered** — **and any time a patrol pulls you over.**

**If you have a dispute with your insurance company:** the Texas Department of Insurance — [1-800-252-3439](tel:+18002523439) · [File a complaint](https://www.tdi.texas.gov/consumer/get-help-with-an-insurance-complaint.html)

blocks.do: An insurance complaint needs: **the policy number, the company name, and what happened with its date.** Have them ready before you open the form.

blocks.h: And a practical question

blocks.p: Will a company sell you insurance without a Social Security number, or with a foreign license? **It differs from company to company** — no law prevents it, but the company may refuse. **Call more than one company, and don't assume the first refusal is the rule.**

blocks.h: Buying from a person instead of a dealership — five rules

ul: **Never buy without the Title in your hand on the day you pay**
**The name on the Title must be the seller's name** — otherwise he is an unlicensed dealer
**30 days to transfer it** — then 25 dollars + 25 for every month you are late, **and no waiver**
**Insurance before registration** — and without proof of insurance the car is not registered
**Check the Title's history officially for two dollars** — TxDMV Title Check

blocks.h: Toll roads — no cash at all

blocks.warn: **The toll road system in Harris County does not take cash.** No booth, no coin basket. **And the managed lanes on I-10 say it outright on the sign: cash is not accepted.**

blocks.p: **Anyone who drives on them without an EZ TAG — and plenty of people do without knowing —** gets a bill in the mail **at a higher rate plus administrative fees**, **and the owner of the car is responsible no matter who was driving**. Then comes a violation notice. **And whoever lets them pile up** is blocked from renewing the registration, is barred from the roads, **and his car can be impounded.**

ul: **Open an EZ TAG account before you drive** — [hctra.org](https://hctra.org) · [281-875-3279](tel:+12818753279)
**And one tag works on every toll road in Texas**
**And you have 90 days to dispute** a violation

blocks.h: If the police stop you while you are driving

blocks.p: **The law requires two things:** show your license, and show proof of insurance, when asked.

ul: Pull over to the far right · Stay in the car · Hands on the wheel
**Tell the officer where your papers are before you reach for them**
**And signing a ticket is not an admission of guilt** — that is what the Department of Public Safety itself says

blocks.warn: **This section changed a lot in 2025 and 2026.** Some federal guidance documents were withdrawn, **but the laws were not touched**. What follows is **only what still stands and is confirmed**.

blocks.h: At the hospital and the clinic — the strongest right left to you

blocks.p: **Interpreting is free and required** at every health care provider that receives federal funding, **and they have no right to ask you to bring your own interpreter or to pay for one**.

ul: **A child is not allowed to interpret for you** — except in a life-threatening emergency, and only for the moment
**Nor an adult companion who is not qualified** — except in an emergency, or if you ask for it yourself **in writing**
**Nor a staff member passing by** who happens to know Arabic

blocks.p: To complain: [Complaint portal](https://ocrportal.hhs.gov/ocr/smartscreen/main.jsf) · [1-877-696-6775](tel:+18776966775) — **and you have 180 days**

blocks.h: At school

blocks.p: Your right stands — see section five. **And start with the Bilingual/ESL department in your school district.** The federal complaint is **within 180 days and you do not need a lawyer** — **and it has been harder since July 2026.**

blocks.h: In court

ul: **Immigration court:** the interpreter is **at the government's expense** — **ask for one thirty days before the hearing**
**Federal court:** free in cases the government brings — **not in private lawsuits between individuals**
**And state courts differ** — ask the court clerk early

blocks.p: **Careful:** the interpreter is free in immigration court — **the lawyer is not**.

blocks.h: "Certified translation" for official papers

blocks.p: What the immigration service asks for: **a complete translation into English**, along with **a signed statement from the translator** saying the translation is complete and accurate and that he is qualified.

ul: ✕ **No government translation license** — no such thing exists
✕ **And no notarized certification** — it is not required
✕ **And no list of certified translators** to choose from

blocks.p: **So anyone who tells you "I am the only certified translator" is selling you an illusion.**

blocks.h: And if you have no right to an interpreter — you hire one

ul: **Agree on the price before the appointment** — usually by the hour and with a minimum
**And ask him: have you handled situations like mine?** A medical interpreter is not a contracts interpreter
**And ask him to interpret your words as they are** — not to answer for you and not to trim what you think
**And do not give your original papers to anyone**

t: Immigration — Who Is Allowed to Advise You

blocks.warn: **Arabna does not give immigration advice, and it never will.** This section does not tell you what to file or whether you qualify — **it tells you how to find someone who is allowed to say that, and how not to get robbed on the way.**

blocks.p: **Why this limit:** giving immigration advice without a license is **a crime**, and wrong advice can cost a person their right to stay. **And no general guide fits your own case.**

blocks.h: Who Is Legally Allowed — Only Two

ul: **A licensed attorney** — a member in good standing of the bar of their state
**An accredited representative** — not a lawyer, but authorized by the DOJ, working at a recognized nonprofit organization

blocks.p: **Other than these two — nobody.** An "immigration consultant," a "paperwork expert," **or a "notario"** — not one of them is authorized to represent you.

blocks.alert: **This particular trick is aimed at us:** back home, a "notario" is an official with legal standing. **In America, a notary public is only allowed to witness a signature** — they know nothing about immigration, **and they have no right to advise you on a single form**. The DOJ has recorded cases where **asylum applications were filed in people's names without their knowledge** — and that alone can destroy a person's case forever.

blocks.h: Six Signs: Walk Away the Moment You See One

ul: ✕ He asks you to **sign a blank page** or one with wrong information on it
✕ He **takes your original documents** and keeps them
✕ He asks to be paid in **gift cards**, by **wire transfer**, or in **cryptocurrency**
✕ He **sells you forms** the government gives out free
✕ His website **does not end in .gov** and he claims to be an official agency
✕ He **guarantees you the result** — nobody can do that

blocks.h: How to Check Before You Pay a Dollar — Three Minutes

ul: **The DOJ roster** by state and city: [The official roster](https://www.justice.gov/eoir/recognized-organizations-and-accredited-representatives-roster-state-and-city) · [703-305-0289](tel:+17033050289)
**For an attorney:** the bar of the **state** where he says he is licensed — **there is no single national registry**

blocks.do: The roster is ordered by state and then by city: **open Texas and read your city.** **And anyone not on this list who is not a lawyer has no right to represent you — whatever their office looks like.**

blocks.p: **Ask for his full name and license number, and tell him you are going to check.** A real one will not mind. **If he minds, he has answered you.**

blocks.h: Free or Low-Cost Help — It Really Exists

ul: **The DOJ list of free legal service providers**: [The list](https://www.justice.gov/eoir/list-pro-bono-legal-service-providers)
**Recognized organizations** may charge a fee, but they are **required to serve low-income people**
**Legal aid** [lawhelp.org](https://www.lawhelp.org) — **careful:** federally funded programs are **limited to certain immigration statuses**

blocks.do: The pro bono list is ordered by state as well — **read it before you pay anyone, not after.**

blocks.h: Three Scams That Target Immigration Only

ul: **Immigration fees paid a strange way:** USCIS **does not accept** Western Union, MoneyGram, PayPal, or gift cards, **and it never asks for payment over the phone**
**The visa lottery:** entering is **free and random**, **and nobody can raise your odds**
**A tax preparer who refuses to sign your return** — **a clear red flag**, and people who file with an ITIN run into it most

blocks.p: **To report:** [uscis.gov/avoid-scams](https://www.uscis.gov/avoid-scams) · [800-375-5283](tel:+18003755283) · and the DOJ at [EOIR.Fraud.Program@usdoj.gov](mailto:EOIR.Fraud.Program@usdoj.gov)

blocks.h: Reporting a Change of Address — Ten Days

blocks.warn: **Every non-citizen must report a change of address to USCIS within 10 days of moving.**

blocks.p: **The trap is not the reporting, it is your pending applications:** reporting online satisfies the law, **but it does not update your pending case unless you enter the receipt number for each application** — forget that, and the decision notice goes to your old address.
**Who is exempt:** A and G visa holders, and visitors on the visa waiver.

**The newcomer is targeted on purpose** — because he does not know the system, and because he has something to lose. **And most scams do not come through immigration. They come through the mail and the phone.**

blocks.h: Four Rules That Save You from Memorizing Every Scam

rows: A government agency **does not call you first to ask for money** — it starts with mail
**Never pay any official agency with a gift card, a wire transfer, or cryptocurrency**
**The rush itself is the scam** — "today or you get fined" is a scammer's line
**Do not call the number printed in the letter** — call the number from the official website

blocks.p: **Rule four is the most useful in practice**, because it works even if the letter is real. **You do not need to know whether it is fake** — you only need to not call the number in it.

blocks.h: "How Did They Get My Number and My Home Address?"

blocks.p: **Nobody hacked anything. The information is public by law:**

ul: **Vehicle registration records** — your name, your address, your car's make and year
**Home ownership records** at the county — completely public
**Business filings** — the owner's name and the mailing address
**Data brokers** collect all of it and sell it as lists

blocks.warn: **That is why you get a letter saying your car warranty is about to expire with your exact make and year in it** — not because they know you, but because your registration is public. **Their knowing the detail is the trick itself:** you assume anyone who knows your car must be your dealer. Same the hour you register a business — **your name and your shop's address go into a public record that same day**, which is why the "labor law poster" mail arrives **after** you open, not before.

blocks.p: **What cuts the volume down — it does not end it:**

blocks.do: At `donotcall.gov`: type your phone number and your email, **and a confirmation link comes to you by email — the registration does not take effect until you click it.** At `optoutprescreen.com`: you choose five years or permanent, **and the permanent one needs a form you sign and mail.**

blocks.p: **The list stops the legitimate seller, not the scammer** — so whoever calls you after you sign up is **more likely to be a scammer, not less**. That is its real value: **the call itself becomes the signal**.

blocks.h: 1) "Your Car Warranty Is About to Expire" — and You Never Had One

ul: **You are not signed up for anything that could expire** — so there is nothing to "renew"
**The sender is not the dealer or the manufacturer** — read the small name at the bottom of the page
**What they sell is a "service contract," not a warranty** — and the difference is not just wording: all the terms and exclusions are in it
**Do not press "press 1 to be removed"** — pressing proves the number is live, so it sells for more

blocks.p: **If you really want to buy one:** sellers of vehicle service contracts in Texas **must be registered** with the Department of Licensing and Regulation — [1-800-803-9202](tel:+18008039202) · [tdlr.texas.gov](https://www.tdlr.texas.gov). **If you cannot find them in the registry, do not pay them.**

blocks.do: Type the company name or its license number to see whether it is current. **And if someone refuses to give you their license number, that is where the matter ends.**

blocks.h: 2) "You Owe Money, and If You Don't Pay We'll Send It to Collections" — a Debt That Does Not Exist

blocks.alert: **Anyone collecting a debt from you must send you a written notice with the details.** **You have thirty days from receiving it to ask for proof in writing** — **and until they prove it, they must stop coming after you.**

ul: **Do not pay anything over the phone**, no matter how hard they push
**Ask for the proof in writing** — not by voice
**Do not give an account number or a card** "to verify your identity"
**Keep a copy of what you sent and when**

blocks.p: **Ready-made letter templates** you fill in and send: [the federal consumer protection agency](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/debt-collection/)
**Threatening you with arrest over a civil debt is a flat lie** — whoever says it has just told you who they are.

blocks.h: 3) "Buy the Labor Law Poster or You'll Be Fined" — This One Is the Clearest

blocks.alert: **Two facts end the matter:** • **The posters are free** — you print them from the Department of Labor and from the Texas Workforce Commission without paying a dollar • **And if you have no employees, you do not need a poster at all** — the posters are addressed to employees, **so if you are the only worker in your shop, you do not need them, free or paid.**

blocks.do: The posters are downloaded and printed free from both sites. **Anyone who sold them to you sold you something that is free.**

blocks.p: **From the same family — mail asking for a fee for a "certificate of standing" or an "annual report":**

ul: **The Certificate of Existence** really costs **$15** from the Secretary of State — anyone asking 80 or 120 is **a middleman selling you a paper you can request yourself**

**And there is no "annual report" for the Secretary of State in Texas** — an LLC files its report with the **Comptroller's office**. **So mail from a private company asking for an "annual report" is the scam itself.**

blocks.h: 4) The Tax Call — Its Season Starts in January

blocks.p: **"You owe the IRS money, we are trying to resolve it, give us your Social Security number."**

ul: **The IRS always starts with mail** — not a call, not a text message, not an email
**It does not ask for your Social Security number on a call**
**It does not threaten arrest, or taking your license, or deportation**
**It does not take gift cards or wire transfers**

blocks.alert: **And the new part that has to be said:** the IRS put **impersonation using AI-generated voices** at **number two** on its list of the worst scams of 2026. **A voice no longer proves anything** — and neither does the number showing on your screen, **which is faked with one click**.

blocks.p: **If you really think you might owe something:** open your account on [IRS.gov](https://www.irs.gov) yourself, **or call the number from the website yourself** — not the number that called you.

blocks.h: 5) Health Insurance Calls — They Spike When Open Enrollment Starts

ul: The only official place to enroll: [healthcare.gov](https://www.healthcare.gov) · [1-800-318-2596](tel:+18003182596)
**What these calls sell is usually not insurance** but a "discount card" or a limited plan — **and the difference shows up at the hospital, not on the day of the sale**
**Do not give your Social Security number or your Medicare number to someone who called you** — **the real agency already has your number**

blocks.h: One Rule Worth Saying Out Loud

blocks.warn: **What stops most people from reporting is fear about their status.** **Reporting a scam is not reporting yourself. It does not require a legal status, and nobody asks about it.**

blocks.h: Where to Report

rows: Local police, and a written report

blocks.do: Every one of these reports needs: **the date, the number or the email it came from, and a copy of the message exactly as it reached you — not a description of it.**

blocks.warn: **The first line is the most important:** everything that reached you **by mail** — the car warranty, the labor poster, the fake debt — is **a federal mail crime**, and it goes to the **Postal Inspectors**, nobody else. **Keep the envelope itself** — the postmark and the address are evidence.

blocks.h: Websites Imitating the Toll Road Authority

blocks.alert: **There are copycat sites around hctra.org** — eztag.us.com · eztaghouston.com · hctra.com.co — **and HCTRA itself published a warning about them.** **There are three official sites and no fourth:** [hctra.org](https://hctra.org) · [txtag.org](https://txtag.org) · [txdot.gov](https://txdot.gov)

t: Work and Your Rights as a Worker

blocks.p: **A newcomer starts working before they drive and before they rent.** This section is about the job itself — not about finding one.

rows: Anything over 40 hours in a week
Paid at one and a half times — counted by the week, not by the month

blocks.h: Wages that were not paid

blocks.p: File a complaint with the Texas Workforce Commission **within 180 days** of the day the wages were due, **and file it online** — [twc.texas.gov](https://twc.texas.gov) · [800-832-9243](tel:+18008329243)

blocks.warn: **The federal Department of Labor:** it enforces the law **regardless of a worker's immigration status**. **There is no fee to file a complaint and no fee for the investigation.** **It talks with callers in more than 200 languages.** — [1-866-487-9243](tel:+18664879243)

blocks.h: Safety at work

blocks.p: **The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA):** a complaint **can be filed in any language**, **it can be filed without your name**, and its website is **in Arabic** — [1-800-321-6742](tel:+18003216742)

blocks.alert: **The strongest rule in this section:** OSHA treats **reporting a worker to the police or to immigration authorities** as retaliation, banned by the text of the law. **The deadline for a retaliation complaint is only 30 days.**

blocks.h: The 1099 trap

blocks.p: **Someone who works under the employer's orders, with the employer's tools, on the employer's hours is an employee, not a contractor.** **The difference costs you:** no overtime pay · **and the full 15.3% self-employment tax falls on you** instead of half of it.

rows: A W-4 form on your hiring day

blocks.alert: **A practical rule:** in Texas **most employers are not required to give you a pay stub.** **So write down your own hours day by day** — that paper of yours is your only proof on the day you file a complaint.

blocks.p: **For anyone with no car in their first months here.**

blocks.h: Who pays half fare and who pays nothing

ul: **Half fare:** students · people 65 to 69 · and people with disabilities
**Free:** people 70 and older · veterans · children under five · **and anyone with a jury summons**

blocks.alert: **The old METRO Q card ended in April 2026** — the new system is RideMETRO, with a card or an app.

ul: **The METRO website shows Arabic through machine translation** — not Arabic written by a person, so you will find broken phrases in it — [ridemetro.org](https://ridemetro.org) · [713-635-4000](tel:+17136354000)
**For people with disabilities:** METROLift door-to-door service after an evaluation — [713-225-0119](tel:+17132250119)

t: Taxes and the Free Help With Them

blocks.warn: **The VITA program prepares your tax return for free**, and one of the eligibility conditions — **and this one is literally about us** — is **taxpayers with limited English**, along with people whose income is under a yearly limit and people with a disability.

rows: [800-906-9887](tel:+18009069887) — locations are updated from February to April

blocks.h: If you need an ITIN with it

blocks.p: **Not every site offers it** — only sites with a **Certifying Acceptance Agent** who fills out the **W-7** form **and hands your original documents back to you on the spot** instead of mailing them. **So ask for that by name when you call.**

blocks.alert: **A red flag:** a tax preparer who **refuses to sign your return** — the law requires them to sign it and to write in their professional number.
